study_type.claude: Mixed methods (4 phases: two questionnaires, semi-structured interviews, focus groups)
study_type.nlm: Mixed methods (4 phases: two questionnaires, semi-structured interviews, focus groups)

research_method.claude: 4-phase mixed methods: questionnaire 1 (enjoyment 1-5, time spent 1-6, open questions), online semi-structured interviews, second (validation, Portuguese) questionnaire, two focus groups; medians/IQR, open and hybrid coding, Spearman correlation with permutation p-values; 173 practitioners (158 questionnaire, 11 interviews, 15 in focus groups)
research_method.nlm: 4-phase mixed methods: 2 questionnaires, semi-structured interviews, focus groups; Spearman correlation with permutation testing; 173 practitioners (158 questionnaire [82 + 75], 11 interviewees, 15 focus-group participants)
research_method.value: Four-phase mixed-methods study: first questionnaire (task enjoyment 1–5, time spent 1–6, open questions), online semi-structured interviews, second validation questionnaire, two online focus groups; medians/IQR, open and hybrid coding, Spearman correlation (permutation p-values); 173 practitioners (158 questionnaire respondents, 11 interviewees, 15 focus-group participants)
research_method.note: Claude flags minor per-phase count inconsistencies in the paper (82 vs 81; 75 vs 77).

context.claude: Industry; practitioners of multiple roles from various companies, mainly Poland and Brazil; focus groups with two teams of a Brazilian finance company (51-200 employees); 173 practitioners
context.nlm: Industry; practitioners in Poland and Brazil across small to large companies; focus groups at a Brazilian finance company; 173 practitioners
context.value: industry; practitioners of multiple roles (developers, managers, QA, data engineers, admins, architects) mainly from Poland and Brazil; focus groups with two teams of one Brazilian finance company (51–200 employees); 173 practitioners

space_applied.note: SPACE only cited (time spent is not productivity).

ai_discussed.note: Claude: study does not involve AI; only a focus-group suggestion to use LLMs for documentation. NotebookLM: LLM-assisted documentation discussed as a positive impact. Full text: one focus-group quote (p. 8) and a three-sentence discussion paragraph (p. 9).

remote_covid.note: Work mode not reported; only data collection was online.

data_window.note: Not stated by either; no collection dates found in the full text.

cat_productivity.note: Productivity only cited from literature (Murphy-Hill, SPACE, Nichols); the authors state time spent is not productivity.

cat_quality.note: Technical debt appears only as a dislike factor.

cat_collaboration.note: Borderline: enjoyment and time spent rated for meetings, code review, helping and interruptions; validated 'individual work vs. teamwork dilemma' and meeting-size findings; no dedicated collaboration metric.

cat_satisfaction.note: Task enjoyment ratings (1–5) for 18 tasks and enjoyment/dislike factors.

cat_activity.note: Both tag self-reported time spent per task (ordinal 1–6) as Activity; it is not repository activity.

cat_devex.note: Both tag enjoyment 'Satisfaction / DevEx'; only Fagerholm & Münch developer experience is referenced, not the DevEx framework.

cat_agile.note: Sprint planning/daily meetings only as taxonomy examples.

cat_survey.note: Two questionnaires with ordinal scales, interviews and focus groups on perceptions.
